claims.text: Program.cs validates every Bearer token with AddJwtBearer: issuer, audience, signing key and lifetime are checked from configuration, with no lookup of any stored login record.
JwtTokenService.IssueToken sets the token to expire 8 hours after issue (expires: DateTime.UtcNow.AddHours(8)).
This app has no code that ends a token before it expires: no revocation list, denylist or logout endpoint exists at stage-1.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: git grep -i 'revok|denylist|logout' over *.cs finds nothing; AuthController has only login

claims.text: A cookie can carry any value the server sets, a session id or a full token; a session id can equally be sent in a request header. The login model is set by whether the server looks up a record, not by the transport.
claims.source_hint: RFC 6265 (cookie value is opaque to the client); RFC 9110 header fields

claims.text: Sessions kept in one API process's memory are lost when it restarts, so clients must log in again. With several copies, either all reach a shared store or each client is always sent to the copy holding its session.
claims.source_hint: refs/aspnetcore-docs: fundamentals/app-state.md (in-memory session provider); performance/caching/distributed.md ('Survives server restarts')

claims.text: With no stored record, a server cannot end one token before its expiry; doing so needs extra server-side state to check each token against, which the token model otherwise avoids.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: Program.cs:22-43 (validation checks signature, issuer, audience, lifetime only); AuthController.cs

claims.text: Deleting a session record makes the next request that carries its id find nothing, so that login ends at once.
claims.source_hint: refs/aspnetcore-docs: fundamentals/app-state.md (session state, ISession.Clear / session removal)

claims.text: When ending a login immediately matters more than avoiding a server-side store, sessions are the simpler fit.
claims.source_hint: follows from claims 9 and 10; condition stated in the sentence

claims.text: In an Authorization header, the Bearer scheme marks the credential that follows as a bearer token - whoever holds it may use it.
claims.source_hint: RFC 6750 section 2.1 (Authorization Request Header Field); ASP.NET Core JwtBearer handler reads this scheme
